approach: Constant velocity means zero acceleration, so no pseudo force acts on the bob and it hangs exactly vertical under gravity and tension alone.

steps.text: The train moves at constant velocity, so its acceleration is zero and no pseudo force acts on the bob in the train's frame.
With no horizontal force, the string hangs vertically downward, and the tension balances the bob's weight.
The ceiling is parallel to the 30° incline, so the normal to the ceiling is tilted 30° away from the true vertical.
steps.equation: normal to ceiling is 30° from vertical

steps.text: Since the string is exactly vertical, the angle between the string and the normal to the ceiling equals the incline angle.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the string must hang perpendicular to the tilted floor (aligned with the incline's normal) gives an angle of 0°, ignoring that constant velocity means no pseudo force at all.
Adding a pseudo force along the slope even though velocity is constant tilts the string from vertical and changes the tension; with zero acceleration there is none, so T = 10 N.
